problems.stem: You wrote a rename rule to add a date prefix to 200 coursework files. What is the safe first step?
options: Run it on all 200 at once to save time
Run it on a copy of two or three files, check the result, then run the full set
Run it twice to be sure
problems.explanation: A small dry run on copies catches a bad pattern before it corrupts all 200 files.

problems.stem: In a spreadsheet you filter to show only 'overdue' rows, delete them, then clear the filter and find other rows missing. What went wrong, and what is safer?
options: Filtering is never safe; never use it
Deleting on a live filter can hit unintended rows; copy the rows you want to keep to a new sheet, or sort instead, then delete
You should have deleted the columns
The spreadsheet needed to be a PDF
problems.explanation: Deleting filtered rows can affect more than what you see. Preserving the kept rows first makes the delete reviewable.

problems.stem: You set an email rule: 'if subject contains class, move to Archive.' A week later you miss an advisor message. What is the fix?
options: Make the rule specific (match the sender plus a precise subject) and check the Archive folder regularly
problems.explanation: An overbroad rule silently buries needed mail. Narrow the match and review the destination folder.

problems.stem: An automation will overwrite your synced project file with a generated version and cannot be undone in the app. What must you confirm first?
options: That the new file has a nicer name
That a backup copy exists and there is version history or an undo path to recover the original
That you run it on a Friday
That the file is under 1 MB
problems.explanation: Irreversible automations need a recovery path. A backup plus version history means a bad run is not permanent.

problems.stem: Provide a concise response that demonstrates this learning objective: Distinguish artifact polish from evidence-based revision.
problems.expected_answer: The response accurately demonstrates the section objective: Distinguish artifact polish from evidence-based revision, using relevant section concepts, evidence, or calculations.
problems.explanation: This direct-evidence item is used when no closed-response item adequately samples the objective. Score it with the section concepts and worked examples as the rubric.
